answers.question: How long before I can run again? A friend wants me to race the Thanksgiving 10K in five weeks.
answers.answer:
You can start jogging about four days after the race, on Thu Oct 22, if walking and stairs feel close to normal. If the quads still make stairs hard that morning, walk again and try Saturday. Short and slow is the goal for the first runs.

The Thanksgiving 10K is realistic. Five weeks leaves two easy weeks, then about three weeks to rebuild with some short, quicker running. Your marathon fitness should carry over, but I would treat it as a fun race rather than a time attempt unless your legs bounce back quickly.

We can decide at the end of the week of Oct 26 – Nov 1, based on how the first runs feel. What do you want from it: race it hard, run it easy with your friend, or skip it and take a longer break?

new.analysis:
The taper went exactly as planned and the race was a strong result, so the job now is recovery, not correction. Every run in race week landed within a tenth of a mile of the plan, and your easy runs sat at 136 to 139 beats per minute as usual. Nothing was skipped or overrun.

The 3:50 missed the 3:45 target by about five minutes, and the splits show where it went. You held about 8:30 per mile through roughly 20 miles, a touch quicker than the 8:35 that 3:45 needs, then slowed to about 9:28 over the closing miles. That points to quad durability more than fitness, which fits a build that was squeezed when the race moved two weeks earlier and reached 20 miles only once.

Heart rate averaged 161 over the race, well above the 145 to 150 on your marathon-pace training runs. Pace costs more over 26 miles than over 4 to 8 miles of training, so that gap is expected. It does not mean your fitness was off.

Recovery runs on a longer clock than how you feel. Energy often returns within days, but sore muscles and the repair under them take one to two weeks. That is why this week is mostly walking with a few short runs, and the next adds easy volume with no quality or strides.

The drop from 41 miles to about 9 is deliberate, and it protects what the build gave you. If you do the 10K, the three weeks after recovery would bring easy volume back toward your usual 30 or so miles, add strides, and fit in one or two short quicker sessions. I will set that once you tell me what you want from the race.

safetyCallouts.title: Soreness should ease every day.
safetyCallouts.body: Sore quads and calves that improve daily are normal after a marathon. If pain gets worse, turns sharp, or stays on one side, stop running and see a physio or doctor. Sudden calf swelling, chest pain, dizziness or shortness of breath needs prompt medical attention.

safetyCallouts.title: Keep an eye on the toe blister.
safetyCallouts.body: If it turns red, hot or swollen, or drains pus, have a doctor or pharmacist look at it. Skip the run if it hurts to push off.
